summary: 新西兰草药使用长期伴随争议，从野外采集是否助长入侵植物，到毛利传统疗法的地位及今天的监管。公众接受部分保健观念，并未消除对证据、产品标准与行业规范的分歧。

paragraphs.brief: 在自然环境中收获植物和草药作为药物使用的做法已存在了很长时间。
sentences: There is an age-old practice of harvesting plants and herbs in their natural environment for use as medicines.
在自然环境中收获植物和草药作为药物使用的做法已存在了很长时间。

And today there is huge potential for New Zealand to develop a herb industry based on the excellent growing conditions and expertise there, according to Phil Rasmussen, a pharmacist and medical herbalist.
据药剂师和药剂师Phil Rasmussen所说，新西兰在目前以生长良好的条件和专门知识为基础发展草药工业的潜力巨大。
Take arnica, for example, a popular pharmaceutical herb used to treat bruises and joint problems.
例如，用阿尼卡药草来治疗瘀伤和共同问题。
Traditionally collected by Romany communities in Europe, it is now in high demand worldwide as interest develops in the capabilities of the small alpine plant.
欧洲的吉普赛人社区历来收集到这种资料，随着人们对小型高山植物的能力产生兴趣，现在全世界对这种资料的需求很大。
A 2008 report for the Plant and Food Research organisation concluded that New Zealand has a good opportunity to cultivate arnica flowers and roots for the international markets.
植物和食品研究组织2008年的一份报告指出，新西兰有很好的机会为国际市场种植芳香花和根。
However, the initiative was stopped in its tracks when the government abruptly halted funding for the research programme.
然而，当政府突然停止为研究方案提供资金时，该倡议就停止了。
It was an unjustified move, according to agronomist Malcolm Douglas, based on a number of inaccurate views about weed invasion.
据农学家Malcolm Douglas称，这是不合理的举动，其依据是对大麻入侵的一些不准确看法。

paragraphs.brief: 新西兰的草药历史长期以来一直存在这种分歧。
sentences: The history of herbal medicines in New Zealand has long featured disagreements of this sort.
新西兰的草药历史长期以来一直存在这种分歧。

For the early Maori people – the original inhabitants of New Zealand – the forest was well stocked with edible plants that were an obvious source of nutrition, but that were taken for the relief of pain as well.
对于早期的毛利人——新西兰的原始居民——来说，森林里有很多食用植物，这些植物显然是营养的来源，但也是为了减轻痛苦。

While the earliest European doctors in New Zealand relied on imported dried herbs, many were keen to include native plants in their practices: in his book published in 1891, herbalist James Neil described manuka and koromiko as among New Zealand’s most valuable herbs.
虽然新西兰最早的欧洲医生依赖进口干草药，但许多人都热衷于将当地植物纳入其实践：在1891年出版的书中，药剂师詹姆斯·尼尔将马努卡和科罗米科描述为新西兰最有价值的草药之一。
Despite its popularity among some, however, herbalism continued to have its detractors.
然而，尽管草药在一些人中受到欢迎，但它继续有诋毁者。
In 1907 Neil, president of the then very young New Zealand Association of Medical Herbalists (NZAMH), petitioned parliament for legal status for herbalists, but he was unsuccessful.
1907年，当时非常年轻的新西兰药草师协会主席尼尔向议会申请药草师的法律地位，但他没有成功。
The Evening Post newspaper perhaps summed up the opposing position by claiming that herbalism ‘is obsolete’.
《晚邮报》称草药疗法“已经过时”，或许正好概括了反对派的立场。

paragraphs.brief: 事实上，传统的毛利医学面临着更坚定的挑战。
sentences: In fact, traditional Maori medicine faced a more determined challenge.
事实上，传统的毛利医学面临着更坚定的挑战。
In 1908 the government passed a controversial law that had the effect of restricting traditional herbal practice, or pushing it underground.
1908年，政府通过了一项有争议的法律，其效果是限制传统草药做法，或将其推向地下。
Then for a brief period in the mid-20th century, herbal medicine was largely ignored, shunned by the majority of the medical profession, and absent from medical school curricula.
然后在20世纪中叶的一段短暂的时间内，草药基本上被忽视，大多数医学专业都回避了，医学院的课程中也没有这种内容。

But a centuries-old tradition was not going to disappear so easily, and in the 1980s the NZAMH was revived, and it became possible to complete a course in herbal medicine at several polytechnics around the country.
但一个几百年的传统不会轻易消失，而在1980年代，NZAMH被复活，并且有可能在全国的一些理工学院完成一个草药课程。
However, the problem remained of how to connect the culture of plant-based medicine with conventional scientific thinking in order to promote herbal use within the general population.
然而，问题仍然是如何将植物医学文化与传统科学思维联系起来，以便在普通人口中促进草药的使用。
For many years, the limited evidence there was that herbal medicines worked was undermined by lack of interest among general practitioners and within the scientific community.
多年来，有限的证据表明，由于全科医生和科学界缺乏兴趣，药草药品的功效受到了破坏。

paragraphs.brief: Sandra Clair的射程也是一样，他说，这种保证是昂贵的，但是，如果你想将草药的治疗方法出口到世界其他地方，则是必要的。
sentences: Today, the ideas of herbalists in the 1980s – eat a varied diet, include lots of fresh fruit and vegetables, recognise stress – are completely accepted by the medical establishment and widely practised in society as a whole.
今天，20世纪80年代的草药主义者思想 — — 食用多种饮食，包括大量新鲜水果和蔬菜，认识到压力 — — 被医学机构完全接受，并在整个社会广泛采用。
Natural health products are big sellers in pharmacies, and global pharmaceutical companies are buying up natural supplement brands or developing their own.
天然保健产品是药房的大卖家，全球制药公司正在购买自然补充品牌或开发自己的品牌。
What’s more, according to Rasmussen, robust clinical trials show that herbal medicine is generally safe – safer than most drugs.
更严重的是，根据拉斯穆森的说法，强健的临床试验表明，草药一般是安全的 — — 比大多数药物都安全。
‘It doesn’t do everything,’ he says, ‘but there’s a lot it does do, particularly in terms of preventative health care.’
”他说，“它并没有做一切事情，但有许多事情要做，特别是在预防性保健方面。
One significant issue for today’s export-oriented herbal medicine producers is the question of how to guarantee standards for consumers in different countries.
对于当今出口导向的草药生产商来说，一个重要问题是如何保障不同国家消费者的标准。
In other words, there is the need for some form of globally recognised system of documentation.
换句话说，需要某种形式的全球承认的文件系统。
Rasmussen’s range of extracts are produced under the Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) scheme, which is respected around the world.
Rasmussen的精炼品是根据全世界都尊重的良好制造做法(GMP)计划制作的。
So too is the range produced by Sandra Clair, who says that such assurance is expensive but necessary if you want to export herbal remedies to the rest of the world.
Sandra Clair的射程也是一样，他说，这种保证是昂贵的，但是，如果你想将草药的治疗方法出口到世界其他地方，则是必要的。

Moves to launch a joint Australia–New Zealand agency to regulate herbal remedies under a single, streamlined licensing process have recently been revived, after being abandoned in 2007 through lack of support in parliament.
在2007年因议会缺乏支持而被抛弃之后，最近又恢复了采取一项行动，建立一个澳大利亚-新西兰联合机构，在单一、简化的许可证发放程序下管理草药补救措施。

paragraphs.brief: 行业内仍有人支持进一步监管。
sentences: There are those in the industry who support further regulation still.
行业内仍有人支持进一步监管。
According to Rasmussen, some herbs should require a prescription from a suitably qualified medical herbalist or doctor.
拉斯穆森认为，一些药草应该要求有适当资格的药剂师或医生开处方。

For example, consumers shouldn’t be able to go to their local supermarket and buy St John’s Wort, according to Rasmussen, because it can interact in harmful ways with at least ten pharmaceutical drugs.
例如，拉斯穆森认为，消费者不能去本地超市购买圣约翰的Wort，因为它可以与至少10种药物进行有害互动。
Isla Burgess, who is part of the International Research Group for the Conservation of Medicinal Plants, agrees that tighter regulation is necessary, but for a different reason.
作为国际保护药用植物研究小组的成员，Isla Burgess同意，必须加紧管制，但原因不同。
‘More than 400,000 tonnes of medicinal and aromatic plants are traded in the world each year,’ says Burgess.
伯吉斯说：“全球每年交易的药用和芳香植物超过 40 万吨。”
‘The great majority of these are harvested from the wild, so they each have an impact on their local ecosystem.’
”这些动物大部分是从野生生物中收获的，所以它们各自对当地生态系统都有影响。
She gives the example of elm trees in the USA, ringbarked and stripped for the growing market for a product called ‘slippery elm’: this endangered tree should be protected.
她举了在美国的树的例子，在一种叫做“滑翔”的产品的增长市场中，被环击和剥光：这棵濒危的树应该受到保护。
But others argue that more regulation would be prohibitively expensive for all but the largest manufacturers – a change, cautions Clair, that would probably put some local companies out of business.
但其他人则认为，除最大的制造商外，更多的监管对所有人来说都代价太高了 — — 改变，提醒Clair，这可能会使一些本地公司停业。
So, for the time being at least, it seems that the topic of herbal medicines will continue to provoke debate.
因此，至少目前看来，草药问题将继续引起辩论。

items.en: a reference to the interest shown by large corporations in herbal remedies
items.zh: 提及大公司对草药补救办法表示的兴趣
items.why: “global pharmaceutical companies…buying up / developing their own”直接表了明大型公司对草药产品的关注与投入。

items.en: examples of the uses of one particular herbal medicine
items.why: 题干要“某一种草药的用途举例”,A 段以 arnica 为例，给出两种用途 ( 淤青、关节问题 )。

items.en: a warning that small companies cannot afford stricter controls of the herbal medicine industry
items.zh: 警告说小公司买不起更严格控制草药业
items.why: “除最大厂商外都负担不起”“让本地公司倒闭”= 对小公司承担不起更严管制的警告。

items.en: a statement by one expert about the effectiveness and limitations of herbal medicines
items.zh: 一位专家就草药的有效性和局限性所作的发言
items.why: 专家 Rasmussen 同时强调有效性 (a lot it does do) 与局限性 (doesn't do everything),与题干完全对应。

items.en: The history of herbal medicines in New Zealand Originally, the Maori people consumed plants to help deal with ________, and also as food.
items.zh: 新西兰毛利人最初既把植物当作食物，也用它们来应对________。
items.why: Maori 人使用植物“缓解疼痛”,与“help deal with…”完美呼应。

items.en: When Europeans settled in the country, a ________ by James Neil showed that some of them also recognised the medicinal value of native plants.
items.zh: 欧洲人定居新西兰后，詹姆斯·尼尔的一份________表明，部分定居者也认识到当地植物的药用价值。
items.why: 回到对应内容“虽然新西兰最早的欧洲医生依赖进口干草药，但许多人都热衷于将当地植物纳入其实践：在1891年出版的书中，药剂师詹姆斯·尼尔将马努卡和科罗米科描述为新西兰最有价值的草药之一”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The following year, the use of herbal medicines was made more difficult because of a new ________, and for a time in the mid-20th century, they were largely ignored.
items.zh: 次年，一项新的________使使用草药变得更加困难。到了 20 世纪中叶，草药一度几乎无人关注。
items.why: 回到对应内容“1908年，政府通过了一项有争议的法律，其效果是限制传统草药做法，或将其推向地下”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Then in the 1980s a number of institutions started offering a ________ in the subject, although for many years there was still little evidence to support their use, because doctors and academics were not interested.
items.zh: 20 世纪 80 年代，多家机构开始提供有关草药的________。但由于医生和学者缺乏兴趣，多年来支持草药疗效的证据依然很少。
items.why: 1980 年代多所院校开始开设课程，与题干一致。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: There ought to be restrictions on where you can buy some herbal medicines.
items.zh: 应该限制你在哪里可以买一些草药

items.en: The authorities stopped supporting one project without a good reason.
items.zh: 当局毫无理由地停止支持一个项目。

items.en: The herbal medicine industry has an effect on the environment where some plant-based medicines are found.
items.zh: 草药业对发现植物药物的环境有影响。

items.en: New Zealand has the human resources and natural environment to grow herbs commercially.
items.zh: 新西兰拥有商业种植草药的人力资源和自然环境。

items.en: It is essential for herbal medicines to have international certification, despite the cost.
items.zh: 草药必须获得国际认证，尽管费用高昂。

points: 题干要“某一种草药的用途举例”,A 段以 arnica 为例，给出两种用途 ( 淤青、关节问题 )。
Maori 人使用植物“缓解疼痛”,与“help deal with…”完美呼应。
clauses: A 2008 report for the Plant and Food Research organisation concluded ….
“that New Zealand has a good opportunity to cultivate arnica flowers and roots for the international markets”补足 concluded 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 concluded 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, many were keen to include native plants in their practices: in his book published in 1891, herbalist James Neil described manuka and koromiko as among New Zealand’s most valuable herbs.
连接词 while 引出“While the earliest European doctors in New Zealand relied on imported dried herbs”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: The popularity of herbs and plants as medicines could be good for New Zealand
草药和植物作为药物的普及对新西兰可能有好处
